peripherals-bom.notes:
FETCH RELIABILITY. Digi-Key blocks curl (403); its keyword-search pages are readable via page-fetch but inconsistently (RTL8153/RTL8156 returned live listings; LAN7801, LAN9500A, eMMC, SODIMM returned only chrome). Mouser blocks curl and fetch (Incapsula captcha/timeouts) — NO Mouser data despite repeated attempts. Octopart, Newark direct, Arrow, TME, Future, oemsecrets, B&H all 403. Findchips.com (Supplyframe) IS fully curl-fetchable and returns per-distributor price ladders (Newark, Farnell, element14, Microchip-direct, LCSC, Win Source) — it carries all bare-IC pricing here. Newegg and CDW are curl-fetchable. Intel ARK is Cloudflare-blocked. TrendForce contract-price series are paywalled: no OEM NAND/DRAM contract prices, the biggest gap.

HEADLINE. Case 2 incremental BOM ~$67-75 retrofit-retail, ~$32-60 OEM-volume, rising to $253-305 retrofit on DDR5 if the partition needs its own DRAM. Against $123-2,006/yr over 3-5yr, the no-dedicated-DRAM variants pay back in 4-7 months even at the low revenue end. Two structural findings: on an already-docked fleet the network leg is ~$0; and DRAM is the only line exceeding a year of revenue — isolate storage physically, memory logically.

platform-nre.notes:
METHOD: curl with browser UA, no WebSearch. Unfetchable this pass: BLS OES (robot denial), GSA CALC (404, decommissioned), DuckDuckGo/Bing HTML, all PCB-fab pricing pages, EE Times. IBS figures came from the primary Semi Engineering articles, not second-hand blogs.

KEY FINDING: the three tiers separate by roughly two orders of magnitude each (firmware ~$10^6-10^7; board respin similar again on top; new silicon ~$10^8). But Tier 3 is likely the wrong number to quote. Semi Engineering's 2023 follow-up shows IBS headlines are first-mover, new-architecture costs, and documents the estimates themselves falling ~3x as a node matures (16nm $310M->$106M; 28nm $85M->$51M). A partition reusing existing IOMMU/SEV/TrustZone silicon is a Tier 1 delta.

AMORTIZATION (computed): $10M NRE / 5M units = $2/unit; / 500k = $20; / 100k = $100. Against $123-$2,006/yr revenue over a 3-5yr life, Tier 1 clears easily at OEM volume; Tier 3 clears only if the partition ships across the whole client line.

CONFIDENCE: Tier 3 rows are solid and fetched. Tier 1 and Tier 2 dollar brackets are UNVERIFIED constructions - no OEM discloses per-feature firmware or board NRE. Do not present those two as sourced.

items.caveat: Schedule, not money, but it is the real cost: 1.5-2.5 years of delayed revenue for an EAL4 boundary.

items.item: Common Criteria at EAL4-comparable depth - vendor-reported total spend, not just lab fees
items.cost: US$1,000,000-$2,500,000 per evaluation
items.source: Wikipedia "Evaluation Assurance Level" (fetched), reporting mid/late-1990s vendor spend on EAL4-comparable evaluations; primary vendor reports not retrieved
items.caveat: 1990s figures, secondary attribution. The gap vs GAO's lab fee is internal engineering and documentation.

items.item: Common Criteria EAL6 - industry rule of thumb per line of code (the Case-3 headline)
items.cost: ~$10,000 per line of code; ~$87M for seL4's ~8,700-line kernel
items.source: Klein et al., SOSP 2009, sec.7: "industry rules-of-thumb of $10k/LOC for Common Criteria EAL6 certification, which would be $87M for seL4" - trustworthy.systems/publications/nicta_full_text/1852.pdf (fetched)
items.caveat: A rule of thumb quoted by the seL4 authors to argue it is bad value. It caps TCB size: 10k LOC of trusted code is a $100M certification.

items.item: FIPS 140-3 - NIST CMVP cost-recovery fee (government's own published price per submission)
items.source: SafeLogic page reproducing the NIST CMVP cost-recovery fee schedule effective 2024-01-01, https://www.safelogic.com/fips-140-3 (fetched). Direct csrc.nist.gov PDF 404'd.
items.caveat: NIST fee only, and only for a first attempt; excludes accredited-lab testing and consulting. Re-verify on csrc.nist.gov before quoting.

items.item: FIPS 140-3 - accredited lab testing plus consulting (the non-NIST part)
items.cost: ~$50,000-$200,000 typical for a first software module validation
items.source: No public lab rate card was fetchable (Corsec's cost article publishes no figures; Lightship and Rycombe cost pages 404'd). Range is my estimate, not fetched.
items.caveat: UNVERIFIED. Do not put in front of an insurer without an actual lab quote.

items.item: FIPS 140-3 - elapsed time and certificate lifecycle
items.cost: 2+ years end-to-end self-driven; 5-year certificate sunset; pre-validated/rebrand route ~2 months
items.source: SafeLogic FIPS 140-3 page (fetched): "can take two+ years"; "expiration date five years into the future"; RapidCert "in only two months"
items.caveat: Source sells the 2-month alternative, so has an interest in the 2-year figure. The 5-year sunset is a CMVP fact.

items.item: FIPS 140-3 - recurring re-validation exposure (certification is not one-and-done)
items.cost: At least annual standards transitions force lab re-review; ~50% of active modules died in the 2022 transition
items.source: SafeLogic FIPS 140-3 page (fetched): "there was a transition in 2022 that roughly 50% of previously active FIPS 140 validated modules did not survive"
items.caveat: The most underrated line item: certification decays and can force a re-spend well before the 5-year sunset.

items.item: Formal verification of an isolation kernel - measured effort, seL4 (gold standard)
items.cost: ~29 py total: 20.5 py correctness (9 reusable tools + 11 seL4-specific), 4.1 security, 2 binary, 2 capDL; kernel 2.2 py
items.source: Klein et al., "Comprehensive Formal Verification of an OS Microkernel", ACM TOCS 32(1) 2014, sec.7.2 and Fig 19 - trustworthy.systems/publications/nicta_full_text/7371.pdf (fetched)
items.caveat: For an ~8,700-LOC C microkernel. Proof effort is ~9x the kernel's own dev effort and scales with TCB size.

items.item: Formal verification - replication cost for a NEW kernel using the same methodology
items.cost: ~6 py of proof, ~8 py total including the kernel - "only twice the SLOCCount estimate" for an unassured system
items.source: Klein et al., SOSP 2009 sec.7 (fetched)
items.caveat: An author estimate, not a measured second project. This is the commons argument: the 9 py of frameworks is already paid for and shared.

items.item: Formal verification - proof MAINTENANCE per significant change (the recurring line)
items.cost: A change touching ~12% of code cost 1.5-2 py to re-verify (~32% of original effort); another change ~1 py (~17%)
items.source: Klein et al., SOSP 2009 sec.7 "The cost of change", and TOCS 2014 (fetched)
items.caveat: Kills naive Case-3 economics: every respin or firmware revision touching the partition re-opens the proof. Budget ~1 py/yr per maintained line.

items.item: Formal verification, dollarized - seL4-equivalent proof of an isolation boundary
items.cost: 20 py x $150k-$250k loaded = $3.0M-$5.1M one-time; replication (8 py) $1.2M-$2.0M; maintenance $150k-$250k/yr
items.source: Derived: seL4 person-year figures (VERIFIED, Klein TOCS 2014) times a fully-loaded formal-methods engineer cost. The $/py is my assumption, not fetched.
items.caveat: py counts are hard, $/py is not. Note it is 17-70x cheaper than the $87M EAL6 rule-of-thumb for the same kernel.

items.item: CASE 1 TOTAL - security-audited software on the same OS and network
items.cost: One-time $50k-$150k (pentest $5k-$50k + SOC 2 first year $30k-$100k); recurring $20k-$110k/yr
items.source: Sum of the VERIFIED items above (Astra pentest; soc2auditors.io / Secureframe / Bright Defense SOC 2)
items.caveat: No certification line at all. If the enterprise already carries SOC 2, the marginal assurance cost is near zero.

items.item: CASE 2 TOTAL - separate VM plus separate NIC/storage, with a certified boundary
items.cost: Case-1 assurance plus CC EAL2-EAL4: lab fee $240k-$560k (inflated), realistic all-in $500k-$2.5M, 1.5-2.5 yrs
items.source: GAO-06-392 Figs 2 and 4 (VERIFIED) plus vendor-reported EAL4 totals (SECONDARY) plus the Case-1 sums
items.caveat: Whether CC is required is a business judgment. If the insurer accepts SOC 2 plus a hypervisor-scoped pentest, Case 2 collapses to roughly Case 1.

items.item: CASE 3 TOTAL - manufacturer-engineered hardware partition, certifiable boundary
items.cost: Proof route $1.2M-$5.1M one-time + $150k-$250k/yr; EAL6 route ~$10k/LOC of TCB (~$87M at 8.7k LOC); FIPS adds $14k-$17k + lab
items.source: Klein TOCS 2014 / SOSP 2009 effort figures (VERIFIED) plus NIST CMVP fee schedule (VERIFIED) plus an assumed $/py
items.caveat: The two routes differ by ~20x. seL4's result is exactly the argument that proof beats EAL6 on both cost and assurance.

items.item: CASE 3 AMORTIZED - assurance cost per machine by OEM shipment volume
items.cost: $3.0M proof over 1M units = $3.00/unit; over 100k = $30/unit; over 10k = $300/unit; $200k/yr upkeep over 1M = $0.20/unit/yr
items.source: Derived from the dollarized seL4 figure; volumes illustrative
items.caveat: Against $123-$2,006/machine/yr revenue, Case-3 assurance is a rounding error at OEM volume. Silicon NRE, not assurance, decides Case 3.

items.item: CASE 1/2 AMORTIZED - assurance cost per machine by enterprise fleet size
items.cost: $60k/yr midpoint over 10,000 machines = $6/machine/yr; over 1,000 = $60; over 100 = $600
items.source: Derived from the VERIFIED SOC 2 plus pentest recurring ranges
items.caveat: At $123/machine/yr revenue, recurring assurance eats ~50% of gross on a 1,000-machine fleet and exceeds it below ~500. This forces aggregation.

audit-and-certification.notes:
METHOD: curl with browser UA only, no WebSearch. Mojeek for URL discovery (Google/DDG served challenges; Mojeek captcha'd after ~6 queries). Refused/404: csrc.nist.gov CMVP fee PDF, gao.gov direct (403, obtained via govinfo.gov), commoncriteriaportal.org, Vanta/Drata/Sprinto, Lightship and Rycombe FIPS cost pages, niap-ccevs.org (JS app).

STRONGEST NUMBERS, fetched and primary/government: GAO-06-392 CC lab fees and durations by EAL, read off rendered chart pages; NIST CMVP cost-recovery fee schedule; Klein et al. seL4 effort (TOCS 2014 Fig 19, SOSP 2009 sec.7) including proof-maintenance figures that dominate lifetime cost and are rarely quoted.

TWO FINDINGS THAT MATTER. (1) seL4's own authors quote $10k/LOC for EAL6 = $87M for their kernel while their proof cost ~20 py: proof is ~an order of magnitude cheaper than certification for stronger assurance, so Case 3 should pitch proof, not EAL. (2) Certification decays: ~50% of active FIPS 140 modules died in the 2022 transition, and a 12% code change cost seL4 1.5-2 py to re-verify.

WEAKEST ITEM: FIPS accredited-lab fees are UNVERIFIED; no lab publishes a rate card.
